Senses.Explanation: The nostrils—the paired openings of the nose. In the corpus the word is deployed overwhelmingly as a person's handle or vulnerable spot: the place by which one is taken hold of, led, possessed, or lost, and by which one holds one's own ground. Attested collocations (allowlisted corpus counts): it is pierced and led like an ox — (穿卻鼻孔) / (穿鼻孔) (29), "pull the nostrils around," (拽轉鼻孔 4), e.g. "already had the nostrils pierced by the whisk" (已被拂子穿卻鼻孔) and "had his nostrils casually pulled around by that layman" (被箇俗漢等閑拽轉鼻孔); it is placed in another's control — "the nostrils are in someone else's hands," (鼻孔在別人手裏 9), (殊不知鼻孔在別人手裏); it is lost — (失卻鼻孔) (11), and asked after as a fault, "why have you lost your nostrils these days?" (你日來因甚失卻鼻孔); it is groped for and found — (摸著鼻孔) (82), (摸著舊時鼻孔)，(依前只在面皮上便見); and it is held up in independence — (鼻孔遼天) (287) / (鼻孔撩天) (208) ("nostrils to the sky"), (人人鼻孔遼天)，(各各壁立千仞). The texts draw the contrast between (鼻孔在別人手裏) (a nose held by another) and (鼻孔遼天)／(撩天) (a nose held to the sky). Xingkong Xingzhen also seeks to "breathe through the same nostrils as the old ones" (與古人同一鼻孔出氣), making the same body opening the shared outlet of a voice. The word carries no gloss in the texts beyond the body-part and its use as this handle or outlet, and neither does this entry.
Senses.Note: One corpus-wide idiom (6246 occ / 386 texts). Its stock distribution warrants a null sense-level MasterName, while every stored occurrence names its exact speaker or reviewed actor. The literal graphs mean the nostrils; the recurring collocations (穿/拽/失卻/摸著/遼天) are the attested pattern — pierced or led like an ox, held by another, lost, groped for, or held to the sky. Not to be confused with the separate compound heads (鼻孔遼天) / (鼻孔撩天), which are their own idioms.

Occurrences.Kwic: 殊不知鼻孔在別人手裏。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Blue Cliff Record of Chan Master Foguo Yuanwu (佛果圜悟禪師碧巖錄). Yuanwu Keqin uses nostrils held in another person's hands as his image for an interlocutor who does not know that another controls him.

Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Chaozong (朝宗禪師語錄), hall address. Chaozong Tongren is the exact speaker: while holding up the fly-whisk he says that assertions of freedom in mind, freedom in phenomena, and several alternatives all have their nostrils pierced by the whisk.

Occurrences.Kwic: 被箇俗漢等閑拽轉鼻孔。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dahui Pujue (大慧普覺禪師語錄), public case commentary. Dahui Zonggao is the exact speaker who says that the layman casually pulled the interlocutor around by the nostrils.

Occurrences.Kwic: 人人鼻孔遼天，各各壁立千仞。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Collection of Guidelines from the Lineage Patriarchs (列祖提綱錄), Fori Yue's incense-reception hall address. Fori Yue is the exact speaker: he says that buddhas and living beings interpenetrate, self and other are equal, everyone's nostrils pierce the sky, and each stands like a thousand-fathom wall.

Occurrences.Kwic: 摸著舊時鼻孔，依前只在面皮上便見。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Xueyan Zuqin (雪巖祖欽禪師語錄), hall discourse. Xueyan Zuqin is the exact speaker who says that the old nostrils, once felt, are still seen on the face.
Recorded Sayings of Venerable Yushan (雨山和尚語錄), examination of a monk. Yushan Shangsi is the exact speaker who asks why the monk has lately lost his nostrils.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師曰我鼻孔被大師𢬟得痛不徹
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Records of Ancient Worthies (古尊宿語錄), Baizhang Huaihai biography. Baizhang Huaihai is the exact speaker: after returning in tears from attending Mazu Daoyi, he tells a fellow attendant that Mazu Daoyi twisted his nostrils painfully.

Occurrences.Kwic: 山僧如此批判，要與古人同一鼻孔出氣。且道諸人還甘麼？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Xingkong Xingzhen (性空臻禪師語錄), case evaluation. Xingkong Xingzhen is the exact speaker who says that his assessment seeks to breathe through the same nostrils as the old ones.

Occurrences.Kwic: 曾摸著鼻孔，知他無面孔耶？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Xuedou Shiqi (雪竇石奇禪師語錄), instruction for the layman Wu Woyin. Shiqi Tongyun is the exact speaker who asks whether Wu knows the faceless person by having felt his nostrils. The TEI header and biography identify Tongyun, styled Shiqi; Xuedou is the monastery name.

Occurrences.Kwic: 不穿鼻孔底牛。有甚禦處。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Five Lamps Meeting the Source (五燈會元), Luopu Yuanan section. Luopu Yuanan is the exact speaker who says that there is no way to control an ox whose nostrils are not pierced.

Occurrences.Kwic: 人人鼻孔撩天，箇箇安家樂業。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Complete Book of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), Gulin Qingmao section. Gulin Qingmao is the exact speaker who says in a New Year's Eve meeting that everyone's nostrils reach the sky and each is settled in home and occupation.
